domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
a is an integer and 0 <= a <= n - 1
the summation index k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n - 1
division by n and division by k are defined (implicitly requiring n != 0 and k != 0, ensured by n > 1 and k >= 1)
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1 and for all integers a with 0 <= a <= n - 1, letting x be the rational a divided by n, we have: E_n of x equals (1 divided by n) times the sum over integers k from 1 to n - 1 of Res_n of (a,k) divided by k.
quantifier_order: for all integer n with n > 1
for all integer a with 0 <= a <= n - 1

variables.name: a
variables.role: inner parameter to the functions E_n and Res_n; constrained by 0 <= a <= n-1

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index with range 1 <= k <= n-1

variables.domain: rationals of the form a divided by n
variables.name: input_x
variables.role: argument to E_n, defined as x = a/n

witness_dependencies: k is not a free witness; it is a bound summation index depending on n through the range 1 <= k <= n - 1
the value Res_n(a,k) depends on both n and a, and also on the summation index k

statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) = (1/n) * sum_{k=1}^{n-1} Res_n(a,k)/k.
